title: Borrow a GPU
story: To test something on a GPU, ask Slurm for an interactive session with one GPU. Check that you can see it, then give it back.

lesson.title: Asking for one GPU
lesson.intro: You never use a GPU on Geiss-01 directly. You ask Slurm for one, and it gives you a shell where that GPU is yours.

parts.note: Ask Slurm to run something now. If nothing is free, it waits in the queue first.
The resource you want: GPUs, and how many (1). Change the number to ask for more.
Connect the job to your keyboard and screen so you can type in it.
What to run in the job: a new shell. You stay in it until you type `exit`.

lesson.why: Eight GPUs are shared by the whole class. Slurm makes sure each one goes to one person at a time, and `exit` hands it back.
lesson.without: `srun --pty bash` without `--gres` still gives you a shell, but with no GPU: `nvidia-smi` says "No devices were found" and GPU tools fail.

tasks.text: Start an interactive job with 1 GPU
Leave the job so the GPU is free again

hints: `srun --gres=gpu:1 --pty bash` starts an interactive shell with one GPU.
Inside it, `nvidia-smi` shows only your GPU. `exit` ends the job.
